questions.stem: What is the term used for the units of inheritance that carry information for a particular trait?
questions.solution: Genes are the units of inheritance that carry information for specific traits. Chromosomes are structures that contain genes, but they are not the units themselves. Proteins and enzymes are not involved in carrying genetic information directly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a trait that Mendel studied in pea plants?
questions.solution: Mendel studied traits in pea plants that had distinct, contrasting forms, such as yellow or green seeds. questions.stem: Which of the following is a true-breeding line?
choices: A plant that shows varying traits in its offspring
A plant that has only one type of trait in its offspring
A plant that produces flowers of different colours
A plant that grows in different environments
questions.solution: A true-breeding line is one that consistently produces offspring with the same traits, indicating that it is homozygous for those traits. A plant that shows varying traits in its offspring or produces flowers of different colors does not exhibit consistent inheritance. A plant that grows in different environments may show variation due to external factors, not genetic stability.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the physical expression of a trait in an organism?
questions.solution: Phenotype refers to the observable physical characteristics of an organism, such as height or color, which result from the interaction of its genetic makeup with the environment. Genotype is the genetic information that determines these traits, allele is a variant form of a gene, and chromosome is a structure that carries genetic material. Therefore, the correct term is phenotype.

questions.stem: What is the term used for genes that are located on the same chromosome and tend to be inherited together?
questions.solution: Linked genes are the term used for genes located on the same chromosome that are inherited together due to their physical proximity. Allelic genes refer to different forms of the same gene, recessive genes are not necessarily linked, and independent genes assort separately during inheritance.

questions.stem: If a carrier female for colour blindness marries a normal male, what is the probability of their son being colour blind?

questions.stem: In a pedigree analysis, if a trait appears in every generation and is present in both males and females, what is the most likely mode of inheritance?
questions.solution: Autosomal dominant traits often appear in every generation and can affect both males and females equally because the gene is located on a non-sex chromosome and only one copy of the gene is needed to express the trait. Autosomal recessive traits often skip generations and require two copies of the gene to be expressed. Mitochondrial traits are inherited only from the mother and do not follow the pattern described.

The phenotypic expression of the gene is always the same for all alleles

The alleles are not always dominant over each other, and the phenotypic expression of the gene can vary depending on the combination of alleles present.

questions.stem: If a true-breeding line of pea plants is self-pollinated for several generations and still shows the same trait, what does this indicate?
choices: The plant has a low mutation rate
The plant is unable to self-pollinate
